tytul: Fermented wild garlic bulbs: why there is no recipe here
wstep: There is no recipe here for fermented wild garlic bulbs. [T:-]

ostrzezenia.tekst: According to BfR, young wild garlic leaves resemble those of the poisonous lily of the valley and the very poisonous autumn crocus; when in doubt, it is better not to eat them. [T:SUS-337]

akapity: According to an Ask Extension expert, fermentation is not an approved, safe method of preserving garlic, and there are currently no validated recipes for fermented garlic. [T:FER-068]
That answer is about garlic; JarAtlas applies the same caution to wild garlic bulbs. [T:-]
All fresh vegetables except most tomatoes are low-acid foods with a pH above 4.6. [T:FER-004]
The whole product needs a minimum, uniform level of acid to prevent the growth of botulism bacteria. [T:FER-003]
According to AGES, wild garlic is also confused with spotted arum, Solomon’s seal and wild tulips. [T:SUS-337]
JarAtlas has found no tested recipe for fermented wild garlic bulbs from a checked source. [T:-]
